transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-04-07 15:00 ET
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Robert Allen (CTO, Silvercrest), Sarah Nguyen (Head of Compliance), Tom Alvarez (InfoSec)

Summary: quick discovery focused on data residency, GDPR/HIPAA controls, log retention and encryption. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deploy - primary concern is where customer data and logs persist and who can access keys.

Topics: data residency (EU/US), HIPAA applicability, audit logs retention, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, RBAC, Dedicated pools, private VPC connector, fallback/replication, demo/benchmarks next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, i'll do a quick intro and then liam will go into some of the technical questions - can i get quick intros from your side?
[00:12] Robert: yeah robert allen, cto at silvercrest, thanks - we have sarah and tom here who'll focus on compliance and security
[00:18] Sarah: hi all, sarah nguyen, head of compliance, primarily concerned about data residency and retention for customer PII
[00:22] Tom: tom alvarez, infosec - i'll ask about logs, keys, and how much telemetry you keep
[00:27] Liam: great, quick outline - we want to understand your current stack, regulatory scope, traffic patterns, and what "no-copy" or private options you need
[00:35] Robert: high level - we are multi-region, core banking in us-east and eu-west, product teams are in the us. we're starting to add LLM features for customer support and document summarization.
[00:47] Robert: primary question: can we use hosted redwood but guarantee data doesn't leave eu for eu customers? and second, how do you handle logs that might contain sensitive text?
[00:58] Maya: short answer: for full EU data residency we generally recommend Dedicated or Private - hosted can be region-restricted for some customers but for strict controls we typically do Dedicated capacity or Private deployment in your VPC. liam i'll let you add technical detail.
[01:12] Liam: yeah, hosted api can be region pinned but note that some control plane artifacts and telemetry may still cross boundaries depending on config - for strict GDPR/HIPAA requirements we do two patterns: dedicated GPU pools in a region with storage and KV cache pinned to that region, or private (on-prem or VPC) where the control plane is separated. there was some chatter about the control plane in hosted but - sorry transcription - the control plane can be customer-managed for private.
[01:35] Sarah: we need to be explicit: logs must not contain full customer documents, retention should be configurable and deletions auditable. also we require SOC2 and HIPAA attestation before pilot.
[01:46] Liam: understood. we offer configurable logging levels: minimal request metadata, full request/response logging (opt-in), and a redaction layer that can mask or drop PII before logs are written. for Dedicated deployments we can disable persistent request logging entirely and maintain only anonymized telemetry for infra metrics.
[02:03] Tom: how do you handle KMS? keys must be customer-controlled ideally in our HSM - we can't have provider-managed keys for certain workflows.
[02:12] Maya: we support KMS integrations, you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via customer-managed KMS - liam can give details on HSM and key lifecycle.
[02:20] Liam: yes BYOK supported - for Private we can integrate with your HSM or cloud KMS; for Dedicated we can do customer-managed keys in the same cloud region. when keys are customer-controlled we limit Redwood employees' access and logs show key usage. note: there's a little complexity around model caching (kv cache) and encryption at rest - we encrypt caches but with BYOK we can ensure keys remain in your control.
[02:40] Robert: what about egress to third-party models or fallback? we need to ensure no data is sent to outside models.
[02:46] Liam: we have routing policies; we can pin to a verified model catalog and disable fallback to external models. for Dedicated/Private you control the model variants that are allowed.
[02:55] Sarah: GDPR also requires data subject access, right to erasure - can we delete all customer prompts and embeddings on request?
[03:02] Liam: yes, with Dedicated/Private we can support full data deletion on demand and provide logs showing deletion operations. hosted api can be configured to not persist prompts but you'd want contractual guarantees for regulated use.
[03:15] Robert: can you talk about logging TTLs? our default policy is 30 days for most logs, 7 years for some audit trails but those must be locked down.
[03:24] Tom: and certain logs cannot contain full text of legal documents - need redaction or hashing.
[03:29] Liam: redaction/masking is supported - we can hash or tokenise fields, or run a pre-ingest redaction pipeline. for long-term audit trails we can store metadata only (who, when, action) and store it in your audit log bucket.
[03:43] Sarah: SSO is mandatory, we need SAML2.0 + SCIM for provisioning and RBAC scoped to teams.
[03:49] Maya: yes SAML and SCIM are supported, and we have role-based access controls - you can restrict who can view logs vs who can manage models.
[03:56] Liam: also we surface audit logs in the console and can stream them to your SIEM via syslog/Kafka or cloud logging sinks. there's an option to send raw logs to your logging bucket so redwood doesn't retain them.
[04:09] Robert: latency is also a consideration - for in-app chat we need sub-400ms p50. how does Dedicated compare to Private for latency?
[04:18] Liam: Dedicated in-region gives predictable latency and throughput; Private in your VPC can be slightly lower latency because it's in your network, but depends on your infra. Dedicated gives us a lot of control over batching and kernel selection - sorry mis-said, kernel selection for performance - we test models and pick quantization and kernel combos for best latency/per-cost.
[04:37] Robert: ok, price will be factor, we'd like to compare hosted per-token vs Dedicated commit vs Private licensing.
[04:44] Maya: we'll send a pricing matrix. typical pattern: start on hosted for non-sensitive features, pilot Dedicated for EU customer traffic, then consider Private for regulated workloads.
[04:55] Sarah: for HIPAA - PHI flows matter. Are you willing to sign a BAA and restrict logs?
[05:02] Maya: we have customers under BAA - we can support BAA, and for PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private with BYOK and disabled logging. we'll include BAA onboarding steps in the docs.
[05:12] Tom: small detail - do you keep model training data or fine-tune on customer data? that's a non-starter unless sanitized.
[05:19] Liam: we don't train customer data into Redwood's shared models. optional fine-tuning workflows are customer-controlled and done entirely in customer environment for Private; hosted fine-tune would be explicit and opt-in with contractual controls.
[05:31] Robert: can you share example network diagrams showing where data lives for each deployment option?
[05:36] Maya: yes liam will attach diagrams for hosted pinned region, Dedicated, and Private VPC/on-prem.
[05:41] Liam: i'll also prepare a table of what is stored where (prompts, caches, logs, telemetry) and what can be disabled.
[05:49] Sarah: one more question: data residency certifications - do you have EU data centers for dedicated pools? and do you support data residency for backups?
[05:57] Liam: we operate in major cloud regions and can provision Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 etc; backups and persistent storage can be pinned to region and have the same encryption controls. for Private, backups remain under your control.
[06:08] Robert: sounds reasonable. any gotchas or limitations we should know about for large batch summarization?
[06:14] Liam: batch jobs often need different resource profiles - we can schedule batch on separate Dedicated queues to avoid interfering with real-time traffic, and caching strategies differ. also note that KV cache has to be treated carefully for PII; we can configure eviction and encryption policies.
[06:30] Maya: ok wrapping up - recap: we'll share SOC2/HIPAA docs, architecture diagrams, pricing options for Dedicated vs Private, and schedule a technical deep dive. customer to share data classification and retention windows.
[06:45] Robert: next step from us: sarah and tom will compile the initial data map and compliance checklist; we'll aim to reconvene after the SE deep dive.
[06:53] Maya: great, i'll follow up with calendar invites and docs, thanks everyone
[06:57] Sarah: thanks
[06:58] Tom: thanks
